explanations: allowedOrgs is a comma-separated string, and enabledFor uses String.includes on it. That is a substring match, so allowing "org-12" also enables "org-1" and "org-2", and allowing "acme-eu" enables "acme". AI triage leaks to organizations that never opted in. The list should be split on commas, trimmed, and compared for exact equality.
load() returns the cached flag while now - at < ttlMs, so each instance keeps the old value for up to ttlMs before refetching. It is not immediate and does not need a restart.

The empty catch swallows the error and execution falls through to ruleBasedQueue and assign with reason "rules". Nothing logs or rethrows, there is no retry, and tier2-urgent is only for urgent priority.
The wildcard branch returns flag.plans.includes(org.plan), so the plans list still filters. It is not unconditional, "*" is handled explicitly, and enterprise is only included if listed.
